title: Conditions of Sale for Air Ticket Fare Brands: Pooled Travel Credit and Its Redemption
content:
**1. The pool.** Travel credits issued from a traveller's cancelled bookings under Air Ticket Fare Brands form one pool in that traveller's name, and a new itinerary may be paid for out of several vouchers at once.

**2. Order of consumption.** Vouchers are consumed in order of expiry, the soonest to lapse first. Where two vouchers lapse on the same date, the one issued earlier is consumed first.

**3. Validity.** A travel credit is applied to a new itinerary only when frozen time is not after the moment the voucher was issued against the traveller's cancelled booking plus the credit validity term of the fare brand that produced it. The question is settled before the credit is applied and on the company's own records of the cancelled booking: the moment the voucher was posted, the voucher code and the expiry date standing with it. The records are read for the voucher whose code is quoted for the redemption; what the traveller recalls of the issue date is not the basis.

**4. Counting the term.** Credit validity is counted in whole calendar months from the voucher issue date, and where the issue day does not exist in the expiry month the voucher lapses on the last day of that month. The comparison runs one way only, against the expiry so reached, and the expiry itself is still inside the term.

**4.1 Illustration on hypothetical dates.** Take a voucher issued on 30 November 2025 whose producing brand carries, hypothetically, a credit validity term of six whole calendar months: it expires on 30 May 2026. A redemption at frozen time on 30 May 2026 is not after that expiry, so the credit is applied; a redemption on 31 May 2026 is after it, so the credit is not applied. On the same hypothetical term, a voucher issued on 31 August 2025 would expire in February 2026, a month having no thirty-first day, and so lapses on 28 February 2026.

**5. Redemption by another person.** A voucher was redeemable only by the traveller it was issued to, unless the fare brand that produced it makes credits transferable. That condition is no longer in force. Every other condition of this extract stands.

**6. Value left over.** Where the pooled value exceeds the price of the new itinerary, the remainder stays on the last voucher touched and keeps that voucher's original expiry. Redemption never extends an expiry.

**7. Value short.** Where the pooled value falls short of the price, the difference is collected in the original form of payment, and a partly paid itinerary is never ticketed.

superseded_clauses: A voucher may only be redeemed by the traveller it was issued to unless the fare brand that produced it makes credits transferable.
